CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
GOVERNMENT 
Department of Youth Affairs  
Budgetary Allocation 
Observation / Recommendation 
1 The Committee observes the expenditure pattern of different schemes run by the Department of 
Youth Affairs. The Committee finds that the speed of expenditure is little slow and a major chunk has 
been kept for the last quarter of the financial year. The Committee is unable to understand that against a 
projected demand of Rs.904.73 crore for the year 2017 -18, it got Rs.550.00 crore at BE which was 
further reduced to Rs.544.95 c rore at RE and the Department still has more than Rs.150 crore to spend. 
The Committee feels that there is a disconnect between projected demand and expenditure. The 
Committee therefore, recommends that the Department should take a cautious approach while making a 
projection and the allocation should also be spent in a time bound manner. 
(Para 7) 
Action Taken 
Noted for compliance. 
Rashtriya Yuva Sashaktikaran Karyakaram (RYSK) 
Observation / Recommendation  
2. The Committee observes that under Rashtriya Yuva Sa shaktikaran Karyakaram (RYSK) there 
are 8 components and each component has got allocation separately. Out of total projected demand of 
Rs.644.05 crore, the Ministry has got Rs.408 crore only and the maximum cut has been affected in 
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sanga than i.e. only Rs.255 crore out of a demand of Rs.471.30 crore. The 
Committee feels that it may affect the programmes of NYKS adversely. The Committee recommends 
that all the programmes of different schemes may run in coherence and budget may be distributed as and 
where required so that the work gets done on time. The Committee further recommends that if the 
budget is required more than the allocated at BE 2018-19 it may be taken up at the RE stage. 
(Para  9) 
Action Taken 
Noted for compliance. 
  

3 
 
 
Observation / Recommendation 
3. The Committee is convinced with the steps taken by the Ministry to restructure the schemes for a 
better coherence and consolidated result. The Committee feels that even in future, the Ministry should 
desist from starting any scheme as stand alone. 
(Para  11) 
Action Taken 
Noted for compliance. 
National Programme for Youth and Adolescent Development (NPYAD) 
Observation / Recommendation 
4. The Committee observed that for NPYAD, the Ministry has been allocated Rs.25 crore of BE 
2018-19 i.e. Rs.1 crore more over RE 2017 -18. The Ministry has exhausted almost the entire amount 
allocated to it. The Committee hopes that NPYAD will keep on doing good job at their hand. 
(Para 23) 
Action Taken 
The Ministry accepts the suggestions. 
 
National Young Leaders Programme 
Observation / Recommendation 
5. The Committee observes that the Ministry has relaxed certain norms for implementation of 
schemes for appropriate utilization of budget meant for the scheme under National Young Leaders 
Programme. The Com mittee finds that the budget has been allocated at BE stage to the tune of Rs.20 
crore, which is around Rs.6 crore more than the RE stage. The Committee recommends that Block level 
programme as well as village level programmes may be conducted regularly an d the fund given for it 
may be spent judiciously. 
(Para 34) 
Action Taken 
Noted for compliance. 
Department of Sports 
Budgetary Allocation 
Observation / Recommendation 
7. The Committee notes the Budget for the Department of Sports for the financial year 2018 -19. 
There is an increase of Rs.181 crores, including the National Programmes of Department of Sports 
“Khelo India” from the last year. As regards the allocations for 20 18-19, the Committee observes that 
against the projected budget estimate that of Rs. 2193.05 crore, the Department has got only Rs.1575.15 
crore i.e. a deficit of Rs.617.90 crore. The Committee wonders how the Department of Sports is going to 
cope-up with such a huge gap between the projected demand and the allocated amount. As the three 
major events of international games viz., Commonwealth Games -2018, Asian games-2019 and Olympic 
Games -2020 are scheduled within two years time, the Committee apprehends, h ow the Department is 

4 
 
going to complete its target of training sportspersons to compete at international level. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Department should take up the matter of budget deficit at RE stage with 
the Ministry of Finance, so  that the preparation for mega events should not suffer due to shortage of 
money. 
(Para  2.3) 
Action Taken 
The Scheme of Assistance to NSFs is the main source of funding for preparation of the national 
teams for Commonwealth Games (CWG), Asian Games and the Olympic Games as well as other major 
international tournaments.   
Keeping in view the increase in activit ies relating to training and participation of Indian athletes 
in mega international events scheduled in 2018-19 the budget allocation would be adequate. However, if 
there be any requirement for more funds under this Scheme, the same will be taken up with M inistry of 
Finance at RE stage. 
Sports Authority of India (SAI) 
Observation / Recommendation 
8. The Committee expresses its concern over the pruning of budget for Sports Authority of India 
(SAI) for the financial year 2018 -19. At RE 2017 -18, it was Rs. 495.73  crore which has been further 
decreased to Rs.429.56 crore against a projected demand of Rs.621 crore. The Committee is aware of 
the role of SAI for the Development  of Sports in the country. The Committee feels that it may be 
difficult for the authority to  run its programme and maintain the existing infrastructure. Hence, the 
Committee recommends that the Department of Sports should make concerted efforts for more budget to 
be allocated to SAI at RE stage for its various development works going on in differ ent parts of the 
country. 
(Para  3.4) 
 
Action Taken 
The Budget of SAI has been streamlined in view of the new scheme of Khelo India. Some of the 
activities of SAI will now be covered under the new scheme. 
Further Recommendation of the Committee 
 The Committee notes the reply submitted by the Department. However, the Committee 
desires to be informed about the activities of SAI which would be covered under the new scheme. 
 
Observation / Recommendation 
9. The Committee feels that there is a need of enhancing the role of SAI in trapping talents from 
tribal, rural and backward areas of the country. The Committee is of the view that it may not be feasible 
to achieve the goal of identifying the Sports talent and train them for major events by SAI alone. The 
Committee suggests that the Department of Sports should explore the possibilities of roping in the 
relevant agencies like, the State Governments and its bodies, Public Sector Undertakings, the Corporate 
Sector etc. extending the SAI’s outreach to those areas. 
(Para  3.7) 
 

5 
 
 
Action Taken 
Apart from other sports promotional schemes implemented by SAI for identification and nurturing of 
sports talent, the Special Area Games Scheme lay emphasis at scouting of natural talent for modern 
competitive sports and games from the inaccessible tribal, rural, coastal and hilly areas of the country.  
The Scheme also envisages tapping of talent from the regions/communities which are either genetically 
or geographically advantageous for excellence in a particular sports discipline. 
 
As pointed out in the 303 rd Report of the Department Related Parliament Standing Committee on HRD 
on Demand for Grants 2018 -19 on Item No. 3 of the ATN, Sports Authority of India has directed its all 
the Regional Heads vide letter dated 23.3.2018 to carry out district wise mapping o f sports talent so that 
sports potential from the tribal, rural and backward areas of the country could be identified and nurtured 
to achieve excellence in the national and international level competitions.  
 
Further, as recommended by the Committee possib ilities to explore roping in the relevant agencies like 
State Govt., PSUs, the Corporate Sector etc. will also be initiated immediately.  Efforts will also be 
made to tie up with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for mapping of sports talent from the specific  tribal 
belts of the country. 
Some PSU’s, corporate  sector etc have contrib uted funds/agreed to contribute  funds for promotion of 
Sports.  
 
          Further, some private partners are providing sponsorship to SAI, in terms of facilities as per 
details for few Academies as under:- 
1. National Swimming Academy at Delhi: - “Talent Identification, Development and Management” 
(TIDM) for SAI National Swimming Academy is being supported by Glenmark Aquatic Foundation 
(GAF) contributing for following: 
i. Talent Identification for SAI NSA –Talent Nurturing – Recruitment & Compensation for Coaching 
& support staff  
ii. Talent Nurturing – Training Programme design & Management  
iii. Talent Nurturing – Athlete Sponsorship  
iv. Advanced foreign training & competition (Amounting to Rs. 1.9 Cr. per year). 
2. National Athletic Academy at Bhopal: - Procam International is contributing following for the SAI 
National Athletics Academy at Bhopal for 5 year w.e.f Jan 2016. 
i. SAI CRC Bhopal is running National Athletic Academy for Middle and Long Distance  from 
December 2014 with PP Partnership with Procam International.   
ii. The Procam International is providing 1 Foreign Coach for the Academy during selection & 
selection camps and also foreign exposure of 6 trainees and 1 coach of National Athletics 
Academy for 6 weeks in Kenya. 
3. National Cycling Academy at Delhi: - World Cycling Centre, Aigle, Switzerland is contributing 
following for the SAI National Cycling Academy at I G Sports Complex  for 5 year w.e.f 2015. 
i. 24 Road Bikes alongwith 24 Helmets received in the Month of October 2015. 
ii. Coaching Course was organized in the current year where 14 Asian Countries took part. 
 
 
National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) 

6 
 
Observation / Recommendation 
10. The Committee observes that the budget for National Dope Testing Laboratory, National Anti-
Doping Agency has been allocated as per projected budget estimate. The Committee is concerned over 
the number of cases found as positive is not coming down over the years. The Committee recommends 
that the Ministry should run Awareness Progra m against Doping more vigorously to wipe out this 
menace completely. 
(Para  5.3) 
Action Taken 
Awareness Programme against doping being conducted from time to time. 
NADA is conducting education/awareness program on anti doping in sports by way of educating the 
sportspersons, coaches and support personnel on the ill effects of doping through teaching 
sessions/seminars/workshops and also dissemination of anti doping information. 
As a result, the number of anti -doping rule violations reduced from an all -time high figure of 123 cases 
in the year 2010 to 73 cases in the year 2016, and 79 during the year 2017. 73nos. of educational 
programs/workshops on anti doping in sports have been organized by NADA in current year, with 
greater emphasis in the year 2017 -18 with  the launch of Mass Athlete Awareness Program Against 
Doping.  
To run anti doping awareness campaign vigorously, NADA has redesigned its existing website having 
new features. To further outreach the stakeholders wrt anti doping education and awareness campaign, 
two agencies/NGOs are empanelled by NADA in current year.  Short anti doping video clips were 
prepared by NADA and the same was aired on television channels for wide publicity amongst 
sportspersons.   
 
National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) 
Observation / Recommendation 
11. The Committee observes that NDTL is performing its duties well and the Committee hopes that 
the NDTL will keep on maintaining its standard and impartiality on Dope Test as per international 
norm. 
(Para  6.2) 
Action Taken 
NDTL will maintain its standard and impartiality on Dope Testing as per WADA guidelines. 
National Sports University(NSU) 
Observation / Recommendation 
12. The Committee is happy to note the facts that a National Sports University is coming up in the 
State of Manipur. The Committee feels that the construction of the University should be completed on 
priority so that it could start functioning soon in full fledged manner. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry would ensure that requisite funds are made available so that this project is completed without 
any interruption. 
(Para 7.4) 
  

7 
 
 
Action Taken 
Pending finalization of NSU Bill, National Sports University Society established under the 
Manipur Societies Registration Act, 1989, have started functioning from the Khuman Lampak Sports 
Complex at Imphal. The Academic Session of 2017 -18 commenced w.e.f. 15th January 2018 with two 
courses namely BPES and B. Sc (Sports Coaching). 
M/s. Hindustan Steelworks Construction Ltd. has been engaged as Project Management 
Construction and the Site Development for main campus at Kautruk is in full swi ng. The Tender for 
Construction of the main Campus is likely be finalized shortly. Till March, 2017 an amount of Rs.23.25 
Crores has been released to HSCL for pre -investment activities. Requisite Fund will be made available 
for construction of NSU Campus. 
 
National Centre for Sports Science & Research(NCSSR) 
Observation / Recommendation 
13. The Committee observes that the budget of Rs.40 crores for 2018 -19 provided for NC SSR 
appears to be adequate and hopes that the additional budget may be provided by the Mini stry as and 
when it is required by the Institute. The Committee is of the view that since the area of the sports science 
and sports medicine have gained importance in the recent times, it is a welcome step in right direction to 
establish such a Research Ce ntre in Sports Science and Sports medicine within a stipulated time frame 
and desires to be apprised of the progress of the developments in the matter time to time. 
(Para  9.3) 
Action Taken 
Proposed budget for National Centre of Sports Science & Research is Rs.34.84 Crores and if additional 
Budget is required, the same will be demanded in Revised Estimates 2018-19. 
Present Status of National Centre for Sports Science & Research (NCSSR), Patiala -  
 Equipment procurement has been done for the centre. 
 Renovation and planning for new building structure is under process.  
 Director in charge has been appointed to look after the NCSSR activity.  
 Faculty and staff for the centre are under induction process.

TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY

 The Committee comprehends that by the time the Action Taken Replies were submitted to

National Sports Federations (NSF) 
Observation / Recommendation 
5. The Committee also observes that everything is not in line as far as the functioning of 
Federations is concerned. Regular elections are not held for various posts and rules are not followed as 
per the instructions laid down for the federations. The Committee is concerned over the matter if the 
federations are not functioning properly, it will cause immense loss to related sportspersons and 
ultimately the sports. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that the Federations

(Para  8.9)

Action Taken 
The Ministry regularly monitors the functioning of the NSFs. As per the provisions of National 
Sports Development Code of India (NSDCI), 2011, NSFs are required to follow, inter -alia, proper  
democratic and healthy management practices to ensure greater accountability and transparency at all 
levels; adherence to age and tenure restrictions of office bearers; and holding of elections as per the 
Model election guidelines issued by the Government ; etc. Whenever NSFs are found not holding 
elections after it has become due, Ministry withhold the annual recognition of such NSFs. Recognition

the teams of such sports disciplines towards their training and participation in the international events. 
 
Further Recommendation of the Committee 
  The Committee strongly recommends that the Department should make sure that 
the National Sport Development Cod e of India, 2011 is followed by the National Sports 
Federations and the requisite conditions of the code are strictly implemented. The Committee 
further recommends that SAI should also have some punitive measures to punish erring National 
Sports Federations.

Training of Elite Athletes and Management Support (TEAMS) 
Observation / Recommendation 
7. The Committee observes that TEAMS wing of SAI is handling the training programmes of 
national probables  in various sports disciplines. The Committee desires that it intensively focuses on the 
designing the training programmes specifically for those games/events in which medal prospects are 
very high at forthcoming international events. 
(Para  10.7) 
Action Taken 
Based on standard of Indian athletes/teams at International level and their probability to win 
medal or give respectable performance at International level,  sports disciplines are being identified and 
categorized in four categories i.e. High Priority,  Priority, General & Others.   Accordingly, sports 
disciplines having high medals prospects at the forthcoming international events are kept under High 
Priority category and major portion of the budget allocated to provide support and allied facilities of 
International standard from the scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federation’s’.  
Preparation of Indian sportsperson / teams for International events including Olympic Games is an 
ongoing process.  Government provides assistance to the elite sportspe rsons preparing for the major 
International events such as Olympic, Asian, Commonwealth Games etc. through its scheme of  Scheme 
of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs) & Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme as per 
the details mentioned below:-  
Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs) 
For preparation of Indian sportsperson and teams for major international events, all requisite 
assistance is provided from the scheme as per the approved Annual Calendar of Training and 
Competition (ACTC) finalised in consultation with the concerned NSF.  
Under the scheme of ‘Assistance to National Sports Federation’s’, identified promising 
sportspersons/teams are provided with all the requisite facilities for their preparations, such as 
wholesome n utritious diet, food supplements, equipments, state -of-the-art infrastructure, lodging & 

19 
 
travelling facilities, services of reputed Indian and Foreign Coaches/Supporting staff, Scientific & 
Medical supports, Sports Kit etc. besides financial assistance for  their abroad training and participation 
in International Competitions in India and abroad.   
Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme 
Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme was introduced by Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports in 
July, 2014 to give focused attention  for better performance of our athletes in Olympic & Paralympic 
Games 2016 and 2020.  
Under the Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme, a high level of individual support is provided 
to identified sportspersons who have performed exceptionally well in internat ional events.  This scheme 
includes a monthly stipend of Rs. 50,000/ - for each athlete.  In addition, support is given for 
personalized coaching from both international and national coaches, support staff, participation in 
international events and purchase of sports equipment. 
Further Recommendation of the Committee 
The Committe e appreciate s the steps taken by  the Department for grooming the 
sportspersons for the international events. The Committee is of the opinion that the views of the 
sportspersons should also be given due importance as it would help government  overcoming the 
shortcomings in the efforts being made by the Department.

Action Taken 
The Ministry is reviewing the progress of Khelo India Scheme time-to-time and concerted efforts

structure for efficient and effective Khelo India Scheme in thoroughly prof essional manner, 9 of the 
twelve verticals are being implemented through SAI and LNIPE. This Ministry is directly implementing 
3 verticals. Further the Ministry is dealing with coordination and monitoring of the entire scheme and 
policy related matters. 
As on date,  538 players have been selected during the 1 st Khelo India School Games 2018 under

Basketball, Boxing, Gymnastics, Judo, Hockey, Kabaddi, Kho -Kho, Football, Shooting, Swimming, 
Volleyball, Wrestling, Weightlifting. The TID is in the process of identifying further talent by the

As regards talent identif ied/ selected so far for further training through the National Talent Search

international level.   
National Sports Development Fund (NSDF)  
Observation / Recommendation 
10. The Committee observe s that National Sports Development Fund (NSDF) is a corpus which 
provides financial assistance to various institutes and sportspersons for development of sports. It has 
given Rs.52.81 crore to such organization/institutes/universities in the year 2017 -18 for various sports

from Private and Public Sector is only RS 60.05 lakh, whereas it was Rs.42.28 crore in the financial year 

21 
 
2016-17. There is a steep  fall in the contribution to  NSDF. The Committee is very much concerned 
about this decline. The Committee desires that the Department should find out the reasons therefore and 
apprise the same to Committee along with the suggestions so as to what can be don e to give it a boost in

The actual contribution received for the period 2017-18 is Rs.1065.05 Lakh. (Till 28.03.2018.)  
For augmenting the contributions to NSDF, the Government is regularly interacting with 
CPSUs/PSBs for contribution to the NSDF. They are also encouraged to contribute to the NSDF under

To make contribution to NSDF at tractive there is 100% exemption from  income tax under 
section 80(G) Income Tax Act 1961.  
The Ministry will organize seminars/workshops in major cities to create awareness about NSDF. 
The Department will also depute its teams to potential donors explainin g them about existence of NSDF

 The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department for creating awareness 
about NSDF among PSUs/PSB s. The Committee , however, would like to suggest that the

CHAPTER-I
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY
GOVERNMENT
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Observation/Recommendation
1. The Committee finds that there is a huge gap between the projected demands and actual
allocations made for the Department. Moreover, this reduced allocation of funds do not match with
the objectives of expansion and growth of Higher Education Sector in the country and this would
also defeat the endeavor to bring excellence in Higher Education. The Committee views that the
allocation needs to be enhanced. (Para 2.5)
Further as regards the widening of gap between the projected demand and outlay for the FY
201819 the Committee conceives that Department should reconsider/review its overall mechanism
right from making the proposed demand till the final expenditure is incurred and also assess the
impact thereof in so far as the implementation of various schemes is concerned. This would be
helpful in making the budget more realistic and making its presence felt on the plan outlay to be
formulated for the Department. (Para 2.6)
The Committee notes that the allocation for Central Universities is inadequate as compared
to their infrastructure, faculty and number of students enrolled. The Committee further notes that
Central Universities have a larger number of students enrolled in them as compared to the technical
and management institute. Therefore, the Department should make efforts for increase in the
funding for the Central Universities at appropriate level, the Committee feels. (Para 2.7)
Action Taken
The Actual allocation for D/O Higher Education for the year 2018-19 is Rs 35010.43 crore.
In addition to this, another Rs 21,000 crore (tentative) will be provided through Higher Education
Financing Agency (HEFA) for rebuilding of Central Education Institutions (CEIs). The allocation of
Budget for Central Government/ Ministries is decided by Department of Expenditure, Ministry of
Finance, on the basis of available resources, expenditure trend and absorptive capacity and other
competitive demands. Based on the actual allocation to the Department of Higher Education, the
scheme-wise allocation is done in consultation with the programme division so as to ensure the
optimum utilization of the resources available.
2

CHAPTER-II
OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
GROSS ENROLMENT RATIO
Observation/Recommendation
1. The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Department for the increase of Gross
Enrolment Ratio. The Committee notes that Gross Enrolment Ratio of SC/ST students at 21.1 and
15.4 respectively, is below the national average of 25.2. This in view, of the Committee, needs to
be further improved by augmenting necessary measures by the Department. The Committee desires
that the Department should ensure that the benefit of scholarships and reservation being provided
to SC/ST/OBC and minority students reach them and thereby result into enhanced GER in these
categories. The Committee, would further like to reiterate that the Department should not only take
steps to bridge the gap between the general category students and the SC/ST/OBC and minorities
students but also take initiatives so that students from these sections do not leave their education
in between. (Para 3.4)
Action Taken
Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship is for College and University students belonging to
economically weaker sections of the society. Under the scheme Central Reservation Policy is
adopted, wherein 15%, 7.5% and 27% of the scholarship is earmarked for SC, ST and OBC
students respectively. Since the inception of the scheme 78633 and 27413 ST students have
benefitted under scheme.
The Government is providing interest subsidy on education loan during the period of moratorium
to the students belonging to economically weaker sections of the society including SC, ST & OBC.
Since the inception of the scheme, 2,16,369 SC students, 66,494 ST students & 9,98,094 OBC
students have benefitted under the scheme.
UGC is implementing the following schemes exclusively for the SC and ST category students:-
1. Post-Doctoral fellowship for SC/ST Candidates
2. PG Scholarship for professional courses for SC/ST candidates
3. Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for SC Candidates
4. Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for ST candidates
Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme is for economically weaker sections of the society
enveloping all categories of the candidates. However it is brought to the notice that all interest
subsidy claims received from Nodal bank (Canara Bank) in respect of SC/ST categories are fully
settled by MHRD. Various proactive measures have been taken by the Ministry as well as IITs to
increase GER. Some of these are as under:
(a) The SC/ST/PH students are getting complete fee waiver.
(b) Reservation of seats as per the GoI norms is followed for admission to various
courses in IITs.
3

4
(c) Relaxation of upper age limit upto 5 years is granted to SC/ST candidates for
admission through JEE.
(d) In case the seats reserved for SC/ST/PwD candidates are not filled completely, a
limited number of candidates are admitted to a one-year Preparatory Course on the
basis of further relaxation of admission criteria. On successful completion of the
course, the students are offered direct admission to the already allotted undergraduate
course without having to appear in JEE(Adv) again.
(e) Free Book Bank facility for a semester is provided to SC/ST students.
(f) Appointment of Liaison Officer to redress the grievance of SC/ST Students.
(g) Basic English language course to improve English competency of weak students
RASHTRIYA UCCHTAR SHIKSHA ABHIYAN (RUSA)
Observation/Recommendation
2. The Committee appreciates that RUSA aims to improve overall quality of existing higher
educational institutions in States by ensuring their conformity to prescribed norms and standards
and adoption of accreditation as a mandatory quality assurance framework. The Committee suggests
that the State Higher Education Council should undertake this process of planning, execution and
evaluation, in addition to other monitoring and capacity building functions and greater emphasis
should be laid on the improvement of the quality of teaching-learning processes in order to produce
employable and competitive graduates, post-graduates and PhDs. The Committee impresses upon
the Department of Higher Education to pursue with the respective State Higher Education Councils
to ensure for development of overall quality of Higher Educational Institutions in the respective
States. (Para 4.10)
Action Taken
RUSA lays great importance on improving quality of higher education in the States. Towards
this end, the Department of Higher Education urges State Governments to undertake various
reforms. These reforms include creation of a State Higher Education Council (SHEC) through an
Act of Legislature in every State. The SHEC plays a pivotal role in the process of analyzing the
States’ higher education needs, State Higher Education Plans, implementation of the scheme and
monitoring its performance in the State.
Under RUSA, the proposals of the States are approved by the SHECs before they are uploaded
on the RUSA portal. RUSA also has various monitoring mechanisms such as RUSA fund tracker,
geotagging etc. which can be utilized by the SHECs for tracking the implementation of the scheme
in the respective States.
SHECs are encouraged to have regular meetings and to ensure the State undertakes reforms
in higher education. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the States with MHRD
clearly lays down the expectations from the States under the scheme.
SW AYAM, E-SHODH SINDHU AND NMEICT
Observation/Recommendation
3. The Committee observes that Knowledge modules based on the personalized needs of the

5
learner would need to be delivered to him /her at the right time with the right content interactively
to take care of his / her aspirations. In due course of time there would be a need to develop and
maintain the knowledge and capability profile of every individual learner / worker. Such a system
would have to be developed in a cost effective manner over a period of time. A proper balance
between content generation, research in critical areas relating to imparting of education and connectivity
for integrating our knowledge with the advancements in other countries is to be attempted. For
this, what is needed is a critical mass of experts in every field working in a networked manner
with dedication. This Mission should ensure the support to such initiatives and build upon the
synergies between various efforts by adopting a holistic approach. (Para 5.5)
Action Taken
SWAYAM-MOOCs -  As per ‘Digital India’ Initiative & Electronic Delivery of Services; the
thrust areas assigned to MHRD is to develop & make available ‘Massive Online Open Courses
(MOOCs)’ to the learners throughout the country. The Ministry of HRD, has accordingly embarked
on a major and new initiative called ‘Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds’
(SWAYAM), which provides one integrated platform and portal for online courses, using information
and communication technology (ICT) and covering all higher education subjects and skill sector
courses to ensure that every student in the country has access to the best quality higher education
at affordable cost. Total courses – 1543, Student Registered – 2250383, Student Enrolled – 3639979.
e-Shodh Sindhu -  The main objective of the e-ShodhSindu: Consortia for Higher Education
E-Resources is to provide access to qualitative electronic resources including full-text, bibliographic
and factual databases to academic institutions at a lower rates of subscription. The major aims and
objectives of the e-Shodh Sindhu are as follows:-
 Setting-up e-Shodh Sindhu: Consortia for Higher Education E-Resources by augmenting
and strengthening activities and services offered by three MHRD-funded Consortia;
 Develop a formidable collection of e-journals, e-journal archives and e-books on perpetual
access basis;
 Monitor and promote usage of e-resources in member universities, colleges and technical
institutions in India through awareness and training programmes;
 Provide access to subscription-based scholarly information (e-books and e-journals) to
all educational institutions;
 Bridge digital divide and move towards an information-rich society;
 Provide access to selected e-resources to additional institutions including open universities
and MHRD-funded institutions that are not covered under existing consortia;
 Take-up additional activities and services that require collaborative platform and are not
being performed by existing Consortia; and
 Moving towards developing a National Electronic Library with electronic journals and
electronic books as its major building blocks.

6
 Currently 10000+ e-journals and 3135000+ e-Books are available. These e-journals and
e-resources are used by 91 CFTIs, 217 Universities, 108 Technical Institutions and
3000+ Colleges. It all has been taken from 20 Resources and 4 Databases.
The INFLIBNET Centre has been assigned the responsibility for execution and operation of
e-Shodh Sindhu. e-Shodh Sindhu (ESS) have further integrated additional features to facilitate
seamless access to e-resources such as: (a) The INFLIBNET Access Management Federation
(INFED) – Shibboleth Authentication and authorization of users. (b) InfiStats -COUNTER & SHUSHI
-Data Service usages compliance. (c) JGatePlus for Document Delivery Service (DDS), Meta
Harvesting and Discovery Services (DS).
Virtual Lab -Virtual lab is web enabled experiments which can be designed for remote
operation and viewing so as to enthuse the curiosity and innovation into students. With the present
day internet and computer technologies the above limitations can no more hamper students and
researchers in enhancing their skills and knowledge. Also, in a country such as ours, costly
instruments and equipment need to be shared with fellow researchers to the extent possible.
This would help in learning basic and advanced concepts through remote experimentation.
Physical distances and the lack of resources make us unable to perform experiments, especially
when they involve sophisticated instruments. Also, good teachers are always a scarce resource.
Web-based and video-based courses address the issue of teaching to some extent.
Conducting joint experiments by two participating institutions and also sharing costly resources
has always been a challenge. Today most equipment have computer interface for control and data
storage. It is possible to design good experiments around some of these equipment, which would
enhance the learning of a student. Internet-based experimentation further permits use of resources
– knowledge, software, and data available on the web, apart from encouraging skilful experiments
being simultaneously performed at points separated in space (and possibly, time).
National Digital Library - Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) has in collaboration
with IIT Kharagpur launched National Digital Library (NDL) on 19/06/2018 under the National
Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT). The objective
of the project is to integrate all the existing digitized and digital contents across educational and
cultural institutions/bodies to provide a single-window access to different groups of users ranging
across the entire population.
NDL will fetch metadata of the contents and store and index these metadata in the National
Digital Library servers so that all the e-contents can be searched and accessed in the full-text by
users through a single window. NDL does not store the actual (full-text) contents in its servers;
instead it gives to users links of respective content hosting sites as part of search results. Users
access contents from respective content hosting sites by clicking these links. As on date its content
is available in 200+ launguages, 1.78 crore content is available, 35 lakhs users are registered, 9000
institutions are using it.
e-Yantra - An MHRD initiative under NMEICT Programme, named “e-Yantra” is implemented
to incorporate Robotics into engineering education with the objective of engaging students through
exciting hands-on application of mathematics, computer science, and engineering principles. All the
projects and code are available on the e-Yantra web-site www.e-yantra.org as open source content.

7
FOSSEE -  FOSSEE project sanctioned to IIT Bombay has been promoting use of open
source software in educational institutions (http://fossee.in). It does through instructional material,
such as spoken tutorials, documentation, such as textbook companions, awareness programmes,
such as conferences, training workshops, and Internships.
SWAYAM PRABHA -  SWAY AM Prabha is an initiative of MHRD to provide 32 high quality
educational channels through DTH (Direct to Home) across the length and breadth of the country
on 24X7 bases. The subscribers of free DTH service of Doordarshan (Free dish) would be able
to view these Educational channels using the same set Top Box and TV. No additional investment
would be required.
The DTH channels of MHRD shall carry curriculum-based content and the programme is
designed in such a way that educational content besides being viewed on TV sets with no recurring
cost. These educational programmes delivered over DTH are also made available through YouTube
as archival data. The information related to channel schedules, subject, archival link etc are available
on SWAYAM Prabha portal (https://swayamprabha.gov.in/) which is developed by INFLIBNET Centre
Gandhinagar.
NKN Connectivity -  1 GBPS Connectivity to universities has been provisioned under NMEICT.
A total of 438 Universities have been connected through 1 Gbps Optical Fiber. For Campus
Connect, the Central share for each of the university in NER States is 90% and for other states
& UTs it is 75%. The remaining is to be paid by respective Universities or Institutions. The MHRD
decided that the campus of Universities having NKN connectivity shall be ‘Wi-Fi enabled’ in a
phased manner.
Observation/Recommendation
4. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that new technologies such as online teaching,
virtual class rooms etc. must be used for enhanced learning experience for the students. The
faculty must be encouraged to leverage ICT for better learning outcomes and also deployed for
assessment of student’ s performance. The information and communication technology needs to be
used as a tool across all institution and necessary infrastructure must be made available to
institutions. (Para 5.6)
Action Taken
For leveraging the potential of ICT, in providing high quality personalized and interactive
knowledge modules over the internet/intranet for all the learners in Higher Education Institutions in
anytime any where mode SW AY AM-MOOCs programme is in progress.
SWAYAM-MOOCs - As per ‘Digital India’ Initiative & Electronic Delivery of Services; the
thrust areas assigned to MHRD is to develop & make available ‘Massive Online Open Courses
(MOOCs)’ to the learners throughout the country. The Ministry of HRD, has accordingly embarked
on a major and new initiative called ‘Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds’
(SWAYAM), which will provide one integrated platform and portal for online courses, using information
and communication technology (ICT) and covering all higher education subjects and skill sector
courses to ensure that every student in the country has access to the best quality higher education
at affordable cost. Total courses – 1543, Student Registered – 2250383, Student Enrolled – 3639979.

8
HIGHER EDUCATION FINANCING AGENCY (HEFA) AND REVITALISING INFRASTRUCTURE
AND SYSTEMS IN EDUCATION (RISE)
Observation/Recommendation
5. The Committee welcomes the proposal for speeding up investments in research and related
infrastructure in premier educational institutions, including health educational institutions through
RISE to the tune of 
` 1 lac crore by 2022 and funding would be provided through HEF A. Further,
HEF A is also expected to fund the two new full fledged SP As and 18 more as part of well established
IITs/NITs/CUs etc and grant loans upto ` 5500 crores in FY 2018-19. The Committee is however ,
constrained to observe that the HEF A which was announced in last year’ s budget speech is yet to
take off. The Committee is not satisfied with the progress made so far . The Committee wishes that

is keen to know the action plan how the target set for next four years which seems to be quite

Higher Education Financing Agency(HEFA) is already operational and has approved loan of
` 2015.90 cr. to 6 IITs and 1 NIT. Expenditure Financing Committee (EFC) Note has been
prepared in consultation with the different Ministry/ Departments/ Organizations.
PRIME MINISTERS SPECIAL SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME FOR J & K
Observation/Recommendation
6. The Committee finds it satisfactory that a number of initiatives have been taken for integrating
the differently-abled students towards mainstream higher education. These initiatives are indeed
major steps for providing equal opportunities to such students. The Committee, however, feels that
initiatives will have more impact if awareness about such facilities is dissipated among the targeted
students. Every conceivable effort has to be made to sensitize such students towards the kind of
opportunities waiting for them. Details of all schemes for differently-abled students should be
mandatorily displayed on the websites of UGC, AICTE and IGNOU and also all categories of
universities. In addition, strict and constant monitoring at all level is also required so as to ensure
that all such initiatives for differentlyabled students are being implemented in the real sense. For
both these aspects, Department being the nodal authority for higher education in the country, will
have to take the lead role. (Para 7.10)
Action Taken
The details of the (scholarship) schemes are available on the respective website.
GLOBAL INITIATIVE OF ACADEMIC NETWORKS (GIAN)
Observation/Recommendation
7. The Committee welcomes this initiative to invite distinguished academicians, entrepreneur’s,
scientists, experts from premier institutions from across the world to teach in higher educational
institutions in India, hence promoting international collaborations and improvements in quality

9
of higher education in India. The Committee, however, would like to recommend that the
Department should provide adequate facilities and research facilities in the premier educational
and scientific institutions so that these institutions not just attract global faculty but also
international students. (Para 9.4)

The objective of the GIAN scheme is mainly to attract foreign faculty to deliver short term
courses and not students.
NATIONAL RESEARCH PROFESSORSHIP
Observation/Recommendation
8. The Committee feels that this scheme of National Research Professorship is a novel scheme
to promote research work in the Higher Educational Institution and widen the frontiers of knowledge

position and also increase the funding for research under the scheme. (Para 10.3)

The entire scheme of National Research Professorship is under re-assessment.

WOMEN EDUCATION
Observation/Recommendation
11. The Com mittee feels that the new Swami Vivekanand scholarship for research in humanities
and social sciences introduced by UGC is a welcome step to encourage women scholars to take
up doctoral studies in humanities and social science. The Committee would however like to be
apprised of the number of scholarships to be awarded and amount to be disbursed under this
scheme. (Para 12.8)
Action Taken
Keeping Swami Vivekananda’s ideas of women education and to achieve and promote girls
education, UGC has introduced Swami Vivekananda Fellowship for Single Girl Child for research
in Social Sciences with an aim to compensate direct costs of higher education especially for such
girls who happen to be the only girl child in their family.
The number of slots under the scheme of Swami Vivekananda Single Girl Child fellowship
for research in Humanities and Social Sciences was 300 at the time of introduction of the scheme.
However, later the upper limit was removed and now it has been kept open-ended to attract eligible
scholars. This scheme is implemented on DBT mode.
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
The financial assistance available under the scheme is as follows:

11
Fellowship @ ` 25,000/-p.m. for Initial two years
@ ` 28,000/-p.m. for remaining tenure
Contingency @ ` 10,000/-p.a. for initial two years
@ ` 20,500/-p.a. for remaining tenure
Escort Reader Assistance ` 2,000/-p.m. in case of PWD candidates
During the financial year 2017-18, a total of 150 beneficiaries were disbursed a grant of
` 4.70 crore.
Observation/Recommendation
12. The Committee points out that Technical education contribute a major share to the overall
education system and play a vital role in the social and economic development of our nation and
believe that women have definite role to play. Technical knowledge is becoming an indispensable
part of our living. Today the advancements made in the field of science and engineering has made
life sophisticated and moreover, has improved the quality of life. These technical fields need the
support of highly qualified experts. Technical Education is instrumental in making the remarkable
contribution to economic growth of the Developing Countries by way of suitable manpower production
according to the needs of the Industry, Society and the Global World as a whole. To produce fully
skilled manpower/ knowledgeable technocrats in the present era of science and technology is the
need of the hour . (Para 12.9)
Action Taken
The Committee’s suggestion regarding skilled manpower / knowledgeable technocrats in the
present era of science and technology is taken care by AICTE by launching outcome based model
curriculum for Under Graduate and Post Graduate students in Engineering and Technology and also
for PGDM and MBA students. AICTE has also come out with comprehensive policy for the training
of technical teachers in AICTE approved institutions, so that, trained faculty may produce fully
skilled manpower/ knowledgeable technocrats.
IITs
IITs are Institutes of National Importance governed under the Institute of Technology Act,
1961 as amended from time to time and imparting world class education in the field of science
and technology. The combined student strength in 23 IITs is 85453. To emphasize the need for
promoting research that is socially relevant and is of use to the end users, two schemes namely
Impacting Research Innovation and Technology (IMPRINT) and Uchhatar Avishkar Yojana (UAY)
have been launched. IMPRINT focuses on research in higher educational institutions, with an
allocation `487.00 crore for a period of three years beginning 2016-17. The cost of the project
is met to the extent of 50% by the MHRD and the remaining 50% by the participating Ministry/
Department. UAY promotes industry sponsored, outcome-oriented research projects with an outlay
of `475.00 crore for a period of two years beginning 2016-17. The project cost is met to the
extent of 50% by the MHRD and 25% each by the Industry and the participating Ministry/
Department. UAY is the best example of industry academia collaboration. In addition to 2 already
approved Research Parks at IIT-Kharagpur and IIT-Bombay, five new Research Parks at IIT-
Kanpur, IIT-Guwahati, IIT-Delhi, IIT-Hyderabad and IISc-Banglore have been approved under the

12
Scheme ‘Start up Initiatives in Higher Education Institutes’. To foster the research activities and
sort out the faculty shortage in CEIs, a new fellowship scheme called PMRF has been approved.
INTEREST SUBSIDY AND CONTRIBUTION FOR GUARANTEE FUNDS
Observation/Recommendation
13. The Committee appreciates the increase in the allocation of fund to this scheme to provide
interest subsidy to education loan to students from economically weaker sections. The Committee
hopes that this scheme is implemented by the Department in an effective manner. The Committee
is also of the view that this scheme would effectively increase the enrolment of students in
Technical/Professional Courses in Higher Educational Institutions across the country by increasing
the affordability. (Para 14.2)
Action Taken
SCHOLARSHIP
To improve the quality education and employability of the students the Central Sector Interest
Subsidy Scheme has been modified, wherein only those eligible students who pursue professional/
technical programmes accredited by NBA or Institutions of National Importance or Centrally Funded
Technical Institutions (CFTIs) are considered eligible under the scheme.
Observation/Recommendation
14. The Committee appreciates the increase in the budget for making 20 world class institutions
both in the public and private sectors. The Committee would also like to recommend that these
world class institutions would be able to provide quality education to domestic students at an
affordable rate and also improve the ranking the selected educational institutions. (Para 15.2)
Action Taken
The recommendations are advisory in nature.

PRIME MINISTERIAL SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME FOR JAMMU AND KASHMIR
Scholarship Schemes
Observation/Recommendation
1. The Committee observes that all these Schemes are meant for providing an opportunity to
students to enable them to complete higher studies and become eligible for teaching in higher
educational institutions and for getting gainful employment in Central/States/private sector services.
The objective behind all these Schemes is very laudable. The Committee can only emphasize that
these schemes need to be administered in the real sense, with the benefit reaching the targeted
beneficiaries. The Committee would like to have an impact assessment of these schemes in the
action taken replies furnished by the Department. (Para 7.9)
Action Taken
The Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students was evaluated
by National University for Education Planning and Administration (NUEP A) wherein it was highlighted
that the scheme has financially helped several poor and meritorious students from different social
categories to pursue higher studies.
To assess the impact of the Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme, a study was carried
out by the Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore. According to the report of the IIM
Bangalore, during the study period, annual growth rate of beneficiaries was 9.5%. Of the total
education loan borrowers, 37% of the borrowers are beneficiaries of the Central Sector Interest
Subsidy Scheme.
MHRD has proposed to setup an Interest Subsidy and Credit Gurantee dashboard by Nodal
Bank (Canara Bank) for the students with real time data from banks on geographical/ socio-
economic/ gender/ institution/ accreditation grade of the institution/ category/ course wise distribution
of loan applications, sanctions, subsidy released and adjusted, loan repayments etc. This dashboard
will ensure effective monitoring and enable the Ministry to measures the outcome of the scheme.
However as on date nearly 25 lakh students have benefitted with a total outlay being ` 9,504.52
crores since the inception of CSIS Scheme.
Further Recommendation
The Committee notes the reply furnished by the Department about the steps taken to
provide opportunities to students from poor financial background in higher educational
institutions. The Committee, however, would like to point out that only 25 lakh students
have benefitted from these schemes. The Committee desires that the Department should
make efforts to repeatedly publicize these schemes in press and media, to augment the
dissemination of information. The Committee also suggests that the students who avail
these schemes should be encouraged to take up research and entrepreneurship.

FACULTY POSITION
Observation/Recommendation
2. The Committee has been voicing its concern from time to time on the acute shortage of
faculty in higher educational institutions across the country. The Committee is anguished to find
out that right from well established Central Universities to those set up recently, State universities
as well as private universities, premier institutions like IITs, NITs and IIMs, this problem has been
continuing as the biggest handicap for the development and growth of Higher Education vis-a-vis
maintaining the quality of education. Situation continues to be grim with no improvement forthcoming
in the near future. The Committee points out that the availability of adequate and qualified faculty
is a pre-requisite for quality education. The Committee is convinced by the steps taken by Department
like increase in the retirement age up to 65 years, improvement of salary structures etc. The
Committee also points out that there can be only two possibilities, either our young students are
not attracted towards the teaching profession or the recruitment process is a prolonged one and
involves too many procedural formalities or both. The Committee feels that both the issues need
to be addressed to on priority basis. The Department being the nodal authority for the entire
country so far as higher education sector is concerned has to take proactive role so as to expedite
the filling up a existing vacancies by drawing a practicable deadline. (Para 8.10)
Action Taken
Keeping in mind the fact that the field of higher education is currently facing an acute
shortage of teachers at all levels and also being aware of the decision of the central government
to expand the base of college and university education significantly through out the country, the
UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Other Academic
Staff in Universities and Colleges and Measures for the Maintenance of Standard in Higher Education,
2010 has extended the age of superannuation to 65 years for teachers in University and College
across the country.
UGC has allowed the University to re-employ superannuated teachers for a maximum period
of five years, i.e. up to 70 years against sanctioned vacant post, if such posts are not filled up
by regular candidates. Also Faculty recruitment has been allowed on Part time basis with the same
selection procedure which is done for regular recruitment.
Intensive efforts are being made to attract talented, bright and qualified young men and
women to college and University jobs. The entry point incentives have been substantially increased.
The UGC Regulations, 2010 has prescribed norms for improvement in service conditions for the
new entrant, in terms of better working and leave conditions, career advancement prospects,
retirement benefits etc.
University Grants Commission has been repeatedly requesting the Central Universities to fill
up the vacant teaching posts at the earliest and give top most priority for identifying the causes
for the vacancies and make concerted efforts to fill up the vacancies as per UGC norms, at an
early date to ensure that the teaching work of the university is not adversely affected. UGC vide
letter dated 27
th February, 2018 has requested the VCs of all Central Universities to prepare a time
bound action plan in addressing this issue.

15
Further Recommendation
The Committee notes the reply furnished by the Department. The Committee further
suggests that the Universities and Central Educational Institutions need to evolve a strategy
to hire the best people and offer them attractive salaries and working conditions to keep
them motivated. Efforts need to be taken to encourage qualified individuals to make a
direct entry at both the Associate and Professor levels. The Committee would like to be
apprised of the impact of the efforts made by UGC and the Universities and other educational
institutions.
Observation/Recommendation
3. The Committee recommends that recruitment process should start well in advance before the
post is vacated so that after retirement the newly recruited person takes up position immediately.
The Ministry should work in tandem with Institutions to have this exercise done on yearly-basis
and recruitment must be complete in advance so that shortage does not develop into crisis. At
the same time, the Department should work out a strategy so as to attract the bright students
to the teaching profession. The Committee also suggests that in order to make the teaching
profession more attractive, the faculty should be encouraged to undertake consultancy and are
given start-up financial support. (Para 8.11)
Action Taken
IITs
As per existing norms, students / Faculty ration in IITs is 10:1. Arising of vacancies and
filling up thereof is a continuous process and the Institutes have been taking various initiative to
attract outstanding candidates for faculty positions. Some of these measures include year round
open advertisements, holding of selection committee meetings through video conferencing, invitation
to alumni, scientist and faculty to reach out to potential candidates, advertisement in international
journals, outstanding young faculty awards, etc. IITs also appoint NRIs and OCIs to the faculty
positions on the same terms and conditions as those of regular faculty. Mobility of faculty from
one Central Educational Institute to another has also been allowed from October, 2014. The
institutions are engaging contract, adjunct and visiting faculty as well as using the online mode of
teaching to overcome these shortages. The salary limit for employment visa to foreign faculty has
also been reduced from US $ 25000 to US$ 14000. Recently government has also approved the
Scheme “Prime Minister Research Fellows (PMRF)” in order to attract bright students into Ph.D.
programmes in IITs and IISC Bangalore. This will address out National priorities at the one hand
and shortage of quality faculty in the premier educational institutions on the other.
NITs
The new Recruitment Rules for faculty in NITs have been amended to accelerate the recruitment
process. Against the vacancy of 3484, NITs have initiated steps to fill up approximately 3254
positions of faculty on regular basis. The institutes are at various stages on recruitment. Six NITs
have completed their recruitment process namely, NIT at Rourkela, Allahabad, Tiruchrappalli, Warangal,
Nagpur and Meghalaya.

16
The recruitment of faculty is a continuous process and the vacancies keep arising due to
retirement, resignation and additional requirement on account of enhanced students’ strength, However
all the NITs are at present in the process of recruiting the vacancies as per the decision of Council
of NITSER on regular intervals. There were some court cases filed by faculty associations of
NITs, which had halted the recruitment process in some of the NITs.
IIMs
Recruitment of faculty posts is a continuous ongoing process in Indian institutes of managements
(IIMs) and institutes recruit the faculty as per their individual requirement and make optimum use
of faculty by mix of permanent, contract and Visiting/Guest faculty. The institutions publish a year
round rolling advertisement to attract faculty. Some of the steps taken by them to fill up the posts
are invitation to alumni, scientists/experts and faculty from India and abroad, advertisements in
international journals, etc. Further, Government has decided to allow faculty working under the
Central Government or Central Autonomous Bodies, to join the newly set up Central Education
Institutes on long-term deputation, for a period of ten years.
Further Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the steps taken by the Department to attract faculty to
the elite engineering and higher educational institutions. The Committee, however, out
witnessing the receipt of low number of applications would like to point that real challenge
is in respect of recruiting faculty for engineering discipline. The Committee recommends
that one of the solutions for attracting talented minds to teaching in Engineering institutions
would be to provide a good initial package and other benefits at par with a corporate job.

4. The Committee is happy to note that new IIMs have been opened in the last few years to
cater to the increasing demand for quality higher technical educational institutions. The Committee,

provision of adequate funds for the development of infrastructure in these higher educational
institutions. (Para 11.5)
Action Taken
The six new IIMs have been established namely IIM Amritsar, IIM Bodhgaya, IIM Nagpur,
IIM Sambalpur, IIM Sirmaur, IIM Visakhapatnam during 2015-16 and IIM Jammu which was
established during 2016-17. All these IIMs started operationalization from transit campus in the
same year in which they were established. These IIMs are fully funded by the Central Government
for development of infrastructure.
Further Recommendation
The Committee observes that the Department should have provided the details of
funding of the new IIMs and also the time line for the operationalization of the campuses
from their own buildings. The Committee would like the Ministry to furnish a detail notes
giving the details of funding and the time line ensuring the operationalization of these IIMs
from their new campuses.

Schemes being run by UGC with a specific focus on women:
Scheme 1 :  “Development of Women’s Studies in Indian Universities and Colleges”
The University Grants Commission (UGC) has promoted, strengthened and given direction to
the Women’s Studies Programme in the country since the VII Plan period. Women’s Studies
Centres have been established in the University System in the VII Plan and have been continued
in the subsequent plan periods.
The main objectives of the scheme are to provide financial assistance to Women Studies
Centres for expansion of Women Studies through teaching, research and field action. Inter disciplinary
approach and theoretical grasp to enhance the understanding of society by highlighting feminist
perspectives on social transformation, development, processes of exploitation and constant interaction
with field reality through field action programmes that feed into academic activity.
At present, 161 Women’s Studies Centres are in existence in various Universities and Colleges.
Scheme 2 : Post Doctoral Fellowship for Women:
The objective of this scheme is to provide an opportunity to unemployed women candidates
having Ph.D Degree to carry out the higher and advanced studies and research in science, engineering
and technology/ humanities and social sciences. The total No. of slots available under the scheme
is 100 per year. The total duration of the fellowship is five years.
The financial assistance available under the scheme is as follows:
Fellowship @ ` 38,800/-p.m.
@ ` 46,500/-p.m. after two years
Contingency @ ` 50,000/-p.a.
Escorts/Reader @ ` 2000/-p.m. (fixed) in cases of PWD (Person with
Assistance disability)
HRA As per Government of India norms
AICTE
PRAGATI Scheme being implemented by AICTE is aimed at providing assistance for advancement
of girls pursuing technical education. Total number of Scholarship are 4000 per Annum (2000 for
Degree and 2000 for Diploma). Two girl child per family are eligible, whose family income is not

18
more than ` 8.00 lakh per annum during the preceding financial year (in case of married girl, the
income of parents/ in-laws, whichever is higher will be considered). The selection of candidate is
made on merit, on the basis of qualifying examination to pursue the respective Technical Degree/
Diploma course from any of the AICTE approved institution.
Amount of Scholarship: Tuition Fee of ` 30000/- or at actual, whichever is less and
` 2000/-per month for 10 months as incidentals charges each year. In case of tuition fee waiver/
reimbursement, students are eligible to get an amount of ` 30000/-for the purchase of Books/
Equipment/Software’s/Laptop/Desktop/Vehicle/Fee paid towards competitive examinations forms/exam.
Reservation-15% for SC, 7.5% for ST and 27% for OBC candidate/applicant.
In IITs also, with a view to improve female enrolment in the B.Tech. Programmes, MHRD
vide Order dated 13-7-2017 issued guidelines to increase female enrollment from the 8% in 2016
to 14% in 2018-19, 17% in 2019-20 and 20% in 2020-21 by creating supernumerary seats.
Further Recommendation
The Committee notes the steps taken by the Department and UGC to increase the
enrolment of women in Higher Education. However, the Committee desires that apart from
the above schemes, the Government should also encourage women pursuing research in
science, and technology to take up entrepreneurship and generate employment.

(PMMMNMTT)

6. The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department through this mission to address

institutional arrangements under various components of the Scheme Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya
National Mission on Teachers and Teaching (PMMMNMTT). Some of the gainful outcomes and
benefits that have accrued from the Scheme are:
 Pre-Service Training of Teachers in Central Universities
 Specialised research in teacher education undergoing in Central Universities
 Professional development, In-Service teacher/faculty training and capacity building done
which were propelled by different training programs conducted by the Centres of Excellence
in Curriculum and pedagogy
 Teaching Resources being developed which can be categorized into ICT enabled, low

Induction training programmes for Faculty and Academic Staff in Central and State Universities,

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Observations/Recommendations
1. As it is evident from the data that there has always been a gap in the overall projected demand
of the Ministry and actual allocation. In the year 2015-16, out of the Ministry's overall projected demand
of 
` 30,807.77 crore only 58 per cent funds were allocated. In the year 2016-17, the fund allocation
was 69 per cent of the projected demand. In the year 2017-18, around 87 per cent of the Ministry's
projected demand was met. For the year 2018-19, about 80 per cent of the Ministry's overall projected
demand has been met. The Committee notes that there has always been a gap between the projected
demand of the Ministry and actual allocation to it. This gap is a cause of serious concern for the
Committee as it ultimately affects the implementation of some of the most important schemes/programmes
of the Ministry, catering to the needs of most vulnerable sections of the society i.e women and children.
Similarly, except for the schemes of Support to Training and Employment Programme (STEP), Ujjawala,
Information and Mass Education, Women Helpline and One Stop Centres Schemes, where allocation has
been as per the projected demand, all other schemes/programmes of the Ministry have been allocated
lesser funds against the projected demands. The Committee feels that either the projected demands of the
Ministry are not realistic or it is not able to convince the Ministry of Finance to get its projected demands
met. In both the cases, it is the implementation of the schemes/programmes that gets affected resulting
in depriving the targeted beneficiaries, the benefits of various schemes/programme. The Ministry may
look into it. The Committee suggests that the Ministry should continue to pursue with the Ministry of
Finance for the requisite funds at appropriate stage(s). (Para 2.3)
Action Taken

INTEGRATED CHILD PROTECTION SCHEME (ICPS)
Observations/Recommendations
5. The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Ministry to deal with the issue of missing children.
However, it cannot be denied that everyday thousands of children are reported missing and many of them
are never found. Therefore, it is imperative that all out efforts be made by all the stakeholders i.e.
Central Government, State/UTs Governments, police and other law enforcement agencies in coordination
with each other to tackle the issue of missing children on the priority basis. The Committee reiterates
its earlier recommendation for establishing separate cells in all the police stations for handling the
missing children cases. Further, as the issue of missing children requires sensitive handling, efforts to
locate them need to be synergized to build an effective and functional system where all the stakeholders
work in a concerted, coordinated and integrated manner. The Committee feels strongly about utilisation
of advanced technologies, skills and training for the same. (Para 4.6)
Action Taken
The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 under section 2 (14) (vii) includes
a "Missing Child" as a 'child in need of care and protection'. The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection
of Children) Model Rules, 2016 (JJ Rules) came into force on 21st September, 2016 which were made
as per provision given under sub-section (1) of section 110 of the JJ Act, 2015. Rule 92 of the JJ Rules,
2016 clearly defines the term "missing child" and also includes a procedure of inquiry regarding a missing
child. In addition to this, the Ministry has prepared the "Standard Operating Procedure on Missing
Children" on 23rd November, 2016 and has issued it to the State Governments.
For the better implementation JJ Act and to tackle the issue of missing children on priority basis
and with sensitivity, this Ministry is implementing a comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme from
the financial year 2009-10 onwards namely, Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS), under which
financial assistance is provided, inter-alia, to State Governments/UT Administrations for setting up and
maintenance of the above mentioned institutions. To implement the Scheme, States are required to
sign a Memorandums of Understanding (MoU) with Government of India and all States/UTs have done
so.
Following measures have been undertaken by the Ministry for providing a priority and sensitive
response to the Missing Children:
• In order to provide outreach services to the missing children or needy children, the Ministry
of Women and Child Development is operating Child helpline no. 1098 which is operational
24/7.

10
• Besides, the Ministry has set up web portals 'TrackChild' and 'Khoya-Paya' under its centrally
sponsored Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) to track the missing and found child.
• In sync with Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Model Rules 2016
& Child Protection Services, the Track Child portal became functional in 2012. It provides a
pan India data base of missing and found children. The portal provides a facility of searching
missing children and matching of missing children with the recovered/found children under the
pre-defined parameters such as name, age, parents details date of missing etc. Further, it
provides details of missing children provided by police and received through KhoyaPaya while
details of found children provided by CWCs/JJBs/CCIs. Separate modules for police and
CWC, JJB and CCIs are getting implemented. Under the Portal, option for searching and
matching of missing and recovered children provided to stakeholders.
The TrackChild Portal is implemented in association with the various stakeholders. It is a
networking and interactive platform to bring a synergy of action and integration among the
various stakeholders such as Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Ministry of Railways, State
Governments/UT Administrations, Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, National
Legal Services Authority, Police, Deptt. of WCD, National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB),
NALSA, SALSA, NCPCR, NHRC, PRIs, NGO andd Citizens etc.
There are two modules on TrackChild; one is used by the Police to upload the information
of a missing child after registering FIR and second module used by CWCs, JJBs, staff of the
CCIs or entering information of a recovered/ found child. The Ministry with the assistance
of NIC has trained different stakeholders all over the country on how to use the software for
uploading information of missing children as well as children residing in the Child Care
Institutions (CCIs). A revised and user friendly version i.e. 2.0 TrackChild was launched for
better connectivity and with enhanced features such as Mobile Application during 2015-16.
The URL of TrackChild is www.trackthemissingchild.gov.in. As on 15/06/2018, out of 16866
Police stations, 11684 are making entries of missing/recovered children in TrackChild. Out of
618 CWCs, 461 are updating records of children and out of 617 JJBs 367 are entering data
of children on TrackChild portal. Out of 6020 CCIs, 4346 are making entries of children in
their care.
• Khoya-Paya: In case of missing child, information is extremely important, and so is speed.
Therefore, it was felt that the use of social media can play a pivotal role in searching missing
children. The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched Khoya-Paya on 2nd June
2015. Khoya-Paya, is an enabling platform, where citizens can report missing children as well
as sightings of their whereabouts without loss of time. Found children can also be reported.
Any citizen can register on KhoyaPaya by using an Indian Mobile number.
Objectives of Khoya-Paya are as follows:
• Immediate reporting of missing and found children.
• Tracking missing children through location based interaction.
• Citizens encouraged to participate in locating missing children.

11
• Locating missing children through site based interaction.
• Restoration of missing children with help of TrackChild data base.
Key features of Khoya-Paya:
• Citizens can upload information on found children.
• It also provides facility for matching the two databases.
• Matching of physical attributes of Missing Children with those Found elsewhere.
• Data of missing and sighted/found children maintained centrally.
• Mobile Application available.
• Citizens were encouraged to provide information of sightings of abandoned, lost children and
those accompanied by suspicious persons.
As on June 15, 2018, more than 8967 users had registered on the Portal and nearly 10,682 cases
of missing- sighted children have been published on the portal.
• Railway CHILDLINES - For Securing Missing, Runaway and Abandoned Children, the Ministry
of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Railways has developed Standard
Operating Procedures (SOPs) to be implemented by Railways for rescue and rehabilitation of
runaway, abandoned, kidnapped, trafficked children via railways with help of CHILDLINE
India Foundation.
In this regard, the first CHILD Help Desk was set up in the year 2015. The CHILD Help Desk
works with railway station authorities for restoration of children of their parents / guardians
or their rehabilitation in the absence of parents/ guardians. From 2015 until Apr. 30, 2018,
CHILD Help Desks are functional at 70 major railway stations and 40315 children were
assisted through the Help Desk.
Awareness campaign via posters in railway coaches was launched in November, 2015. Around
2 lakh posters have been put in trains which caution passengers about children around them
who may need protection. Children are brought for temporary stay before they are restored
to their parents or are sent to children's home. Continuous announcements along with
advertisements on the Rail Neer Bottles are being made for passengers to keep a lookout for
such children.
• Expansion of CHILDLINE: CHILDLINE is a nation-wide initiative for rescuing and assisting
children in distress conditions. In the last four years, CHILDLINE (1098 helpline number) has
been extended to 420 locations from 279 (in 2013-14) locations and will be expanded to 80
new locations. With the expanded reach, CHILDLINE has been able to help lakhs of children
and restore them to their families. Phone calls to the helpline have also increased from 38 lakhs
(in 2013-14) to 1.8 crore calls in 2017-18.
• Further as per direction of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India WP (C) 75/2012 BBA vs Union
of India dated 13.1.2015. The Ministry of Women and Child Development has developed a

12
Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for tracing of Missing Children to be used by the
different Stakeholders to follow uniform procedure across the country in searching and
rehabilitation of missing children. The SOP for missing children was issued on 23rd November,

Action Taken
National Nutrition Mission aims to achieve improvement in nutritional status of Children, pregnant
women and lactating mothers and reduce anemia among children and women. It strives to reduce the
level of stunting, under-nutrition, anemia and low birth weight babies. Implementation strategy would be
based on intense monitoring and Convergence Action Plan right upto the grass root level. NNM targets
to reduce stunting, under-nutrition, anemia (among young children, women and adolescent girls) and
reduce low birth weight by 2%, 2%, 3% and 2% per annum respectively. Although the target to reduce
Stunting is atleast 2% p.a., Mission would strive to achieve reduction in Stunting from 38.4% (NFHS-
4) to 25% by 2022 (Mission 25 by 2022).
A sum of `584.60 crore were released to the States/UTs under NNM in the fourth quarter of
2017-18. National level meeting, workshop and video Conference have been organised with States/UTs
to ensure effective implementation of NNM.
The National Mission has been constituted to provide policy support and guidance to the States/UTs,
with an empowered structure called the Executive Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Mo-
WCD. The Executive Committee is an Apex body set up for nutrition related activities (for children below
six years age, AGs and PW&LM) providing direction, policy and guidance for implementation of various

20
programmes/schemes under the NNM. The Executive Committee to meet once in every three months
and will report to the National Council on India's Nutrition Challenges.
A National Council on India's Nutrition Challenges has been constituted for (a) policy direction (b)
review; and (c) effective coordination and convergence between Ministries which all will have a sectoral
responsibility for the challenge of nutrition. The Council shall submit report to the Prime Minister every
6 months.The first meeting of the Executive Committee which is the Apex body under NNM has been
conducted on 13.03.2018. Also the first meeting of the National Council on India's Nutritional Challenges
under the Chairmanship of Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog has been held on 18.04.2018.
